Prophage-encoded acetyltransferases increase the resistance of *K. pneumoniae* to superinfection by O-acetylating the capsular polysaccharide to sterically hinder the adsorption of competing phages that require non-acetylated residues for recognition.

Prophage-encoded SGNH-domain tail-fibre esterases enable infection of O-acetylated Klebsiella capsules by removing acetyl modifications, and catalytic inactivation of these enzymes in isogenic temperate phages abolishes infection of acetylated hosts while enzymatic complementation or prior capsule deacetylation restores it.

Prophage-encoded SGNH-domain tail fibres require catalytic esterase activity to infect *Klebsiella pneumoniae* strains whose capsules are O-acetylated, and mutation of their active-site serine abolishes plaque formation on acetylated hosts but not on genetically matched non-acetylated hosts.

Prophage-encoded SGNH-domain deacetylases in K. pneumoniae function as superinfection exclusion factors by removing O-acetyl groups from the capsular polysaccharide, thereby blocking adsorption of competing virulent phages that require acetylated capsule epitopes for infection.

Prophage-encoded SGNH-domain deacetylases enable infection of K. pneumoniae strains whose capsules carry O-acetyl modifications that block canonical β-helix depolymerases, and their activity simultaneously reshapes host susceptibility to superinfecting virulent phages.

Temperate *Klebsiella pneumoniae* prophages encoding SGNH-domain receptor-binding proteins deacetylate the host capsule to confer superinfection exclusion against β-helix depolymerase-containing virulent phages, such that deletion or inactivation of the prophage-encoded SGNH gene increases adsorption and productive infection by those virulent phages.

Expression of prophage-encoded SGNH-domain deacetylases on the surface of lysogenic Klebsiella pneumoniae alters the capsule O-acetylation profile, increasing susceptibility to virulent depolymerase phages that target deacetylated capsule epitopes while decreasing susceptibility to phages that require acetylated epitopes.

Prophage-encoded SGNH-domain capsule deacetylases confer superinfection exclusion by reducing adsorption of virulent phages whose depolymerases require O-acetylated capsule epitopes for host recognition.
